messages:
leah (DevEx): quick note: customer hit a nasty edge during key rotation — sample app started returning 403s even though project key was rotated. repro below.
omar (SDK): ouch. was REDWOOD_API_KEY still in the image? that'll trump project key in current logic if REDWOOD_PROJECT is present?
leah (DevEx): yes image had REDWOOD_API_KEY baked in and REDWOOD_PROJECT set. after we rolled in REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY, the app kept using the old org key and failed. conf was confusing for the user.
kevin (Ops): server shows "scope_mismatch" in logs but UI only surfaced generic 403. can we make the server response explicit? at least include detail: token not valid for project <name>.
omar (SDK): agreed — two fixes: 1) flip env precedence so PROJECT_KEY beats API_KEY when REDWOOD_PROJECT is set, 2) add a `redwood doctor --auth` check to warn when both keys are present. I'll open a tiny patch.
leah (DevEx): also suggest SDK emit a one-time startup warning: "Both REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY set; if REDWOOD_PROJECT is configured, project key will be used". saves a ton of support noise.
kevin (Ops): on the infra side we'll return structured JSON on auth failures: `{code: "auth_scope_mismatch", detail: "token not valid for project"}` and add header `x-redwood-scope: project`. that should let SDKs display targeted messages.
omar (SDK): will also stop auto-retrying on 403/401 from auth errors. only retry on 429/5xx. otherwise rotation creates request storms.
docs-bot: doc-suggestion: quickstart -> add "Rotation checklist" note + link to `redwood doctor` - PR created: #348
leah (DevEx): thanks team. small followup: can we add a short snippet in the quickstart that shows env precedence table? new users keep getting burned.
omar (SDK): sure, I'll include it in the release notes for sdk-go and sdk-js. cutting patch now.
